calls.title: Close<>GrowthBook - Demo Discussion
calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Analysis: Close × GrowthBook Demo Discussion

Call on [date of demo] with Jake Heier (GrowthBook Account Manager), Logan Bates (GrowthBook Technical Lead), and Alli Leong (GrowthBook observer) meeting with Max Pollack (Engineering Manager, Growth Team), Corey Nilan (Front End Engineer, Growth Team), Lauren W. (Product Manager, Growth & Activation), Elise (Analytics Engineer, Data Team/Snowflake owner), Lauren Schuman (VP of Product Growth), and two additional team members from Close.

## Quantifiable Outcomes & Metrics
The discussion focused on establishing warehouse-native experimentation capabilities but did not yield specific quantifiable targets. Close currently uses Amplitude for analytics via Segment integration, suggesting they process significant experimental data volumes. The primary metric of success appears to be reducing time spent on manual data processes and enabling self-serve product workflows, though specific time-savings targets were not articulated.

## Budget Authority & Decision Signals
Lauren Schuman's presence as VP of Product Growth indicates executive-level budget authority. Max Pollack, as Engineering Manager, serves as the internal champion coordinating the evaluation. The attendance of cross-functional stakeholders (product, engineering, analytics, data) suggests a comprehensive procurement process with multiple approval layers required.

## Technical Requirements & Implementation Complexity
Close identified several critical technical requirements: warehouse-native experimentation on Snowflake with sticky bucketing capabilities, organization-level assignments beyond user-level bucketing, and integration with their existing Snowflake warehouse. Elise's ownership of Snowflake emphasized data infrastructure concerns as a gating factor. Thu Young raised concerns about implementation differences between their current Amplitude/Segment stack and GrowthBook's warehouse-native approach, indicating migration complexity will significantly influence the decision.

## Decision Process & Timeline
The meeting structure suggests Close follows a structured evaluation process. Max previously connected with Jake for discovery; this demo served as the formal product evaluation. The mention of "one or two other people" Max invited but who didn't attend indicates decisions require broader organizational input beyond those present.

## Specific Pain Points
The primary pain point is operational data fragmentation—Close currently sends data to Amplitude via Segment rather than maintaining a centralized warehouse-native approach. This creates inefficiencies in analysis and restricts self-service analytics for product teams. The desire for organization-level bucketing beyond user-level suggests limitations in their current experimentation infrastructure.

## Champion Signals
Max demonstrated strong champion behavior by pre-aligning on focus areas with Jake and driving internal attendance. Lauren W. actively participated by requesting product analytics evaluation despite it being "new this summer," indicating genuine evaluation engagement. Elise's focused participation around Snowflake compatibility reflects technical champion alignment.

## Competitors Mentioned
GrowthBook's competitors were referenced obliquely—Jake noted "a number of our competitors get acquired" and positioning GrowthBook's open-source status as future-proofing against this uncertainty. No specific competitor names were mentioned.

## Next Steps
The demo would proceed with walkthroughs of warehouse-native experimentation workflows, product analytics capabilities, and implementation requirements within Snowflake. GrowthBook committed to demonstrating differences between their approach and Close's current Amplitude/Segment integration, including warehouse-side implementation requirements.
